title: Hash map with chaining
statement: Start simple: Build a string-to-int map with put, get, contains, and size. Collisions chain in buckets. Putting an existing key replaces its value and does not change size. The theory is optional. The C solution appears after the hidden tests pass.
constraints: Resize when size exceeds the bucket count.
think: A hash code chooses a bucket, not the stored entry.
Two keys can land in the same bucket, so each bucket needs a chain.
Equality, not just the hash, decides whether a key is present.
Resize rebuilds every chain because bucket indexes change.
hints: On resize, reinsert every existing entry.

tests.name: put-get
tests.call: { OpenMap m = new OpenMap(); m.put("a", 1); return String.valueOf(m.get("a")); }

tests.name: replace
tests.call: { OpenMap m = new OpenMap(); m.put("a", 1); m.put("a", 4); return m.size() + ":" + m.get("a"); }

tests.name: two
tests.call: { OpenMap m = new OpenMap(); m.put("a", 1); m.put("b", 2); return m.get("a") + "," + m.get("b"); }

tests.name: many
tests.call: { OpenMap m = new OpenMap(); for (int i = 0; i < 30; i++) m.put("k" + i, i); return m.size() + ":" + m.get("k29"); }

tests.name: zero
tests.call: { OpenMap m = new OpenMap(); m.put("z", 0); return String.valueOf(m.get("z")); }

objective: Resolve collisions and replace existing keys without corrupting map size.
workedExample: Hash a key to a bucket, then walk that bucket's chain comparing keys rather than assuming one key per bucket.
On an existing key, replace its value and leave size unchanged; on a new key, link a node and increment size.
recallPrompt: What observation distinguishes replacing a key from inserting a new key?

misconceptions.explanation: A bucket index narrows the search but does not prove key equality.
misconceptions.retry: Describe the comparison required after two keys choose the same bucket.

misconceptions.explanation: Replacing an existing mapping does not add an entry.
misconceptions.retry: Trace size before and after put on the same key twice.

reflectionPrompt: Why does collision handling preserve average lookup time only when buckets stay short?
